newsitem.title: USA: Miss. court rules tobacco Medicaid suit can proceed.
newsitem.headline: Miss. court rules tobacco Medicaid suit can proceed.

text.p: In a blow to the tobacco industry, Mississippi's highest court on Thursday ruled that the first state Medicaid suit seeking to recoup health care costs of smokers can go to trial.
The Mississippi Supreme Court threw out challenges by Gov. Kirk Fordice and the tobacco industry that would have kept the $940 million historic case from proceeding to trial on June 2.
Mississippi became the first state to file a Medicaid suit on May 23, 1994. Since that time, a total of 22 attorneys general and the lieutenant governor of Alabama have filed similar suits.

"They've given us the green light to go to trial. It is the best we could have hoped for," Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore, who filed the suit, told Reuters in a telephone interview. "They threw the governor out of court. They threw the tobacco companies out of court."

Fordice, a Republican, challenged the suit, claiming that only he had the authority to bring lawsuits to recover Medicaid money since the state's division of Medicaid is under the control of his office.
If the court had ruled in Fordice's favour, Moore's lawsuit would have been limited to claims on behalf of charity hospital spending and the prohibition of cigarette advertising aimed at children.
